Nothing in this box is field-replaceable except the air filter, so there are no bays but that one.","kind":"base","part-numbers":{"AS5915-18X-O-48V-S":{"part":"F0PEC5627001Z"}}}},"description":"6x 10G SFP+, 8x 1G SFP and 4x 1G RJ-45 compact cell site gateway, sold as the CSR200, Broadcom BCM88272 Qumran-UX with an Intel Atom C3308 and a Stratum 3E OCXO. Temperature hardened to -40 to 70 C in a 240 mm-deep 1RU shell, side-to-side airflow with an optional air filter, and built-in fixed DC supplies and fans rather than removable ones. Ports number from 1; all timing, management and power connections are on the front.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["rear","top","bottom","left","right"],"wanted":"A figure or square-on photograph of any face but the front. Both staged documents draw the front only - the datasheet's page-2 elevation is the sole elevation in either - so the rear panel here is bare metal. The quick start places a grounding point \"on the device's rear panel or side panel\" and ships a grounding kit of a lug, two screws and two washers, but pictures neither panel, so the lug is not placed: its face is known to exist and its position is not known at all. Airflow is side-to-side, so the left and right panels carry the intake and exhaust and are the faces that matter most here.","what":"rear-elevation"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"An LED table. Neither document has one. Six system lamps are legible on the faceplate - LOC, DIAG, PSU1, PSU2, FAN, ALARM - and the only colour either document states is in the quick start's step 5: \"After power on, the PSU1/PSU2 LEDs should be on green\". So every lamp on this device carries `off` and one green `on`, which is what is known, and the real vocabularies - what amber on DIAG means, what ALARM signals, whether LOC is a locator beacon - are unwritten rather than guessed. The same silence covers BITS, PPS, LINK and ACT.","what":"led-vocabularies"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"Which of each port's two bezel lamps is link and which is activity. Every optical column carries four lamps - two pointing up to its top port, two pointing down to its bottom port - measured consistently across all seven columns of both blocks. Nothing in either document names them, so they are `led-port-N-1` and `led-port-N-2` in the order they are printed, left to right.","what":"port-lamp-roles"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"A picture of the air filter. Edgecore sells two accessories against the filter bay - F0OEC5627002Z, \"Assembled module with filter installed\", and F0OEC5627001Z, \"Air filter frame for field replacement\" - and NEITHER IS PICTURED. Only the slot cover that ships in the bay is drawn, so the bay accepts that cover alone. The filter's own face is a second module waiting on a source.","what":"air-filter-module"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"The maker and part number of the three-pole barrier terminal block. common/dc-terminal-27@1 was created for this device and measured off this device's own elevation - 28.0 x 15.2 on an 8.5 pole pitch, read twice because the face carries two of them - but no document names the bought-in part, and its depth is estimated outright because a front elevation fixes nothing behind the face.","what":"dc-terminal-block-part"},{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["front"],"wanted":"A dimension for the four timing jacks. The elevation supports the CENTRES, which read on a 14.17 pitch, and not the envelope: what is bright in the art is the gold collar at about 3.4 mm, and the nut's flats are dark metal against a dark panel. So the pitch is measured and the part's own size is borrowed.","what":"coax-jack-size"}],"groups":{"filter":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Filter"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"leds":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster - the 1000BASE-T RJ-45 and the RS-232 console share one bezel at the right-hand end, and the USB-A storage port sits apart from them under the first SFP+ shell. The datasheet lists them as four separate callouts; they are one function.","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","lint":{"waive":{"L61":"Eleven marks on this face are printed BESIDE the part they name rather than centred on it, and all eleven positions are measured off the elevation at 9.6341 px/mm. THE COAX LEGENDS ARE EIGHT OF THEM. Each timing pair prints `IN OUT` on one baseline with `1PPS` or `10MHz` under it, and the whole legend sits BETWEEN and BELOW the two jacks: the jacks' centres read 37.97 and the legend's baselines 37.20 and 39.50. The rule measures each word against the single jack it names and sees a 0.77 mm vertical miss, but the word is not trying to centre on that jack - it is one half of a legend centred on the PAIR, which is why `1PPS` is further out than `IN` is. Moving them onto the jack centres would put the legend across the jacks, which is neither what the metal says nor what the rule wants. THE RJ-45 NUMERAL GROUP IS THE OTHER. `17 (up)(down) 18` is printed centred on its METAL CELL - the arrow pair lands at 317.41 against a cell centred at 317.41 - while the rule compares it with the CUTOUT, whose centre is 1.27 mm left because the 8P8C opening is not centred in a rj45-ganged cell. The numerals on the neighbouring column are placed by the same generated rule and pass. Centring on the bore would move a measured mark to quieten a rule."}},"manufacturer":"Edgecore","maturity":"modelled","model":"AS5915-18X","name":"csr200","portfolio":{"family":"Cell Site Router","line":"Service Provider","series":"CSR200"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"airflow":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - \"Supports side-to-side airflow SKU (with Air Filter option)\", and the single published ordering code AS5915-18X-O-48V-S ends in -S for side-to-side. That is why the face carries a filter slot at one end and a perforated field across the middle rather than intake vents at the top and bottom: air crosses the box. No front-to-back SKU is published and none is assumed."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - \"Dimensions (WxDxH): 440 x 240 x 44 mm (17.32 x 9.45 x 1.73 in)\" (csr200-datasheet/doc.md). The quick start's hardware specification says \"440 x 240 x 43.7 mm\", and THE DISAGREEMENT IS 0.3 MM ON ONE AXIS - the two documents agree on width and depth to the digit and on weight at 3.8 kg. That is a rounding of the same metal, not two products, so it is not recorded as sources-disagree; 44.0 is taken because it is the figure the measured figure is scaled against and because a 1RU opening is 44.45. 440 is the body width: the datasheet's own \"Installations to standard 19\", 21\" and 23\" rack\" makes the brackets an accessory outside it, so nothing is subtracted here and the rack ears are optional placements at the library's 14 mm."},"figure-choice":{"confidence":"measured","note":"Gate 1, AND THE PREPARED BRIEF WAS NO HELP AT ALL. The extractor classified the datasheet's page-2 elevation - fig-0012, the only elevation either document contains - as a BANNER and dropped it, which is the exact failure docs/modelling-a-device.md warns about. It was recovered by rendering page 2 at 600 dpi with pdftocairo and finding the panel by row/column darkness: (361,1987)-(4599,2402), 4239 x 416 px. THE FIGURE IS A RENDER, NOT A DRAWING. Its aspect is 10.1899 against 10.0 for 440/44, 1.86 percent out - inside the four percent at which docs/modelling-a-device.md still allows fractions - and the art says the same thing the arithmetic does: the top cage row shows more of its interior than the bottom row. So x carries geometry directly at 9.6341 px/mm anchored on the stated 440 mm, and every y is a proportion of the panel's own 416 px height mapped onto 44 mm, or a registry figure anchored on one such proportion. THERE IS ONLY ONE ELEVATION. Neither document draws the rear, the sides or the top of this chassis, and the quick start says only that the grounding point is \"on the device's rear panel or side panel\" without picturing either. The rear is therefore a bare panel and the omission is recorded in gaps as needs-drawing, rather than furnished by analogy with a sibling that was never measured against it."},"leds":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"The six system lamps read on a 6.986 pitch from 193.89 to 228.82, and their legends - LOC, DIAG, PSU1, PSU2, FAN, ALARM - are legible in the elevation. WHAT THEY MEAN IS NOT DOCUMENTED. Neither document carries an LED table; the quick start states exactly one colour, \"After power on, the PSU1/PSU2 LEDs should be on green\", and that is the only lamp vocabulary either document supports. So every lamp here carries `off` and a single green `on`, and the real vocabularies are recorded as a gap rather than invented from what a similar switch does. THE PORT LAMPS ARE FOUR PER COLUMN, NOT TWO. Each shell's bezel carries `(down) (up) (down) (up)` - two lamps for the upper port and two for the lower - measured on all seven columns of both blocks. Which of each pair is link and which is activity is not stated anywhere, so they are numbered 1 and 2 and the question is in gaps."},"panel-layout":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"Every x below is a reading of the 600 dpi page at 9.6341 px/mm, and the two port blocks check each other. The SFP block's four columns were located by their bezel lamps, whose offsets inside a shell read 2.42/5.27/9.01/11.81 on all four columns to within 0.06 mm; that fixes the column pitch at 14.25, which is the registry's sfp-ganged pitch to the hundredth, and the block origin at 232.87. The SFP+ shells were located the same way and come out on a 27.56 pitch - one 14.25 cage plus a 13.31 gutter of vent field - with the three shells agreeing to 0.11 mm across twelve lamps. THE NUMERALS CONFIRM THE ORIGINS INDEPENDENTLY. Each column prints `n (up)(down) n+1` on one baseline, and the arrow pair's centre lands on the cell centre: 156.20 against a cell centred at 156.21, and 240.00 against 240.00. The RJ-45 block was anchored the same way, giving a 13.93 pitch against the registry's 13.97."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"THE SUPPLIES ARE NOT MODULES. The datasheet's callout 7 is \"PSU 1/PSU 2 (fixed)\" and the key features say \"Load sharing, redundant 48VDC PSUs\" and \"Built-in redundant fan modules\"; the only orderable SKU is \"Fixed Dual DC PSUs\". What is on the face is two three-pole barrier terminal blocks, not two bays, so nothing here is hot-swappable and there are no PSU or fan bays to accept anything. Ratings are the quick start's: 48 VDC, 180 W per supply, 36-72 V 6 A input, and 119 W maximum consumption at 25 C for the box. The datasheet's \"Power Capacity: 180 W (Maximum)\" is the supply's, not the chassis's."},"rows":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"The two cage rows and the bezel between them read 5.36-15.76 and 20.10-30.78 down a shell, so the pair spans 25.4 about a centre at 17.93. Row pitch is the registry's 15.0 for the optical blocks rather than the 14.74 that subtraction gives, because docs/modelling-a-device.md makes ganged pitch a lookup; the top row is then placed at 5.23 so the PAIR stays centred on its measurement. The RJ-45 blocks span 5.08-30.78, which no registry row-pitch covers, so 14.70 there is measured and said to be."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"Two documents, both staged and both docling-converted, but MEASURED OFF THE PDF PAGE RATHER THAN THE CONVERTED FIGURES. csr200-datasheet (the CSR200 / AS5915-18X data sheet) carries the specification list, the ordering matrix, the accessory part numbers and the twelve-callout front elevation on page 2 that every horizontal number here is read from. csr200-qsg is the AS5915-18X quick start guide and supplies the hardware-specification table, the DC ratings, the grounding and timing procedures, and the one sentence that settles what the four coax jacks are: \"Use coax cables to connect the 1-pulse-per-second (1PPS) in/out SMB ports to other synchronized devices.\""},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the port lamps, which point up over down: the 7 SFP pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-13/port-14)."}},"references":[{"sha256":"cf94ced5f4d344f50d591c800d317e6a4d57c9af9527fd093ceec25c271eaf3e","title":"Edgecore CSR200 / AS5915-18X Cell Site Router Data Sheet"},{"sha256":"1d6d7d2905674e0e6d8c6f118262b036d37053523bebcbb0ee50b29da9ae8b42","title":"Edgecore AS5915-18X Cell Site Gateway Quick Start Guide"}],"version":"1.0.5","views":{"bottom":{"empty":"Not drawn by any staged source.
